senses.gloss:
(I)--a Mind-born son of ब्रह्मा, born of his thumb, and father of मूर्ति. A progenitor and guardian of the world, born for the creation of worldly beings.
1: भा. III. १२. २२-3; Ib. II. 6. ४२; 7. 6; Br. II. ३२. ९६; ३६. ८४; Ib. III. 3. ३०; ६५. २१; Ib. IV. 2. ३३, ४७; M. 3. 9; 8. 4; १५४. ३५३; १७१. २७, ४९; वा. २५. 2, ८२, ९०; Vi. I. २२. 4; IV. 1. 6.
Married प्रसूती, daughter of स्वायम्भुव Manu. Had sixteen daughters of whom he gave thirteen to Dharma, one to Agni, one to पितृस्, and one to शिव.
2: भा. III. १२. ५६; Ib. IV. 1. ११, ४७-9; Vi. I. 7. १९-27; Br. I. 1. ५६-64; Ib. II. ३७. ३८-50;.
To the Satra of विश्वसृक् Daks2a came and was welcomed by all standing, except ब्रह्मा and शिव. On this दक्ष burst into anger against शिव and insulted him saying he had eyes like a monkey, was a breaker of law and convention, lord of the भूतस् and गणस्; he then cursed that शिव should have no more share in sacri- fices and went away. Nandi got enraged at this and im- precated a curse on दक्ष that he would lose all knowledge of आत्मन्, and assuming the face of a sheep, would become dull-witted. भृगु then pronounced a counter-curse that those propitiating शिव shall become पाखण्डस्.
3: भा. IV. 2 (whole). M. १३. ११-55, ६०; १८३. २२-3.
Appointed by ब्रह्मा as the overlord of all प्रजापतिस्, दक्ष began the sacrifice of बृहस्पतिसव to which all gods went in groups. सती also expressed her desire to go and requested permission of शिव, who reminded her of the insult offered to him.
4: Ib. IV. 3. (whole).
As she was persistent, she was allowed to attend. Going, she found that she was not properly welcomed by her father. The enraged सती sat facing the northern direction in yoga and cast off her body by means of the fire of समाधी to the distress of gods and others. On this the गण followers of सती attacked दक्ष, when भृगु created a class of gods, ऋभुस् who vanquished these गणस्.
5: Ib. IV. 4 (whole).
Having heard of all this from नारद, शिव grew angry; out of his anger sprang वीरभद्र who was ordered to ruin दक्ष's sacrifice. The beard of भृगु was cut off, and दक्ष's head was severed from his body and thrown into the दक्षिणाग्नि.
6: Ib. IV. 5 (whole). वा. ३० (whole).
The Gods waited upon ब्रह्मा who proceeded to कैलास. He conciliat- ed शिव and pleaded for the revival of दक्ष and continuation of his यज्ञ promising a share to him.
7: भा. IV. 6 (whole).
शिव agreed but [page२-059+ ४३] said that दक्ष should have the face of the sheep, Bhaga, Mitra's eye, and भृगु the beard of a sheep. Agreeing to this ब्रह्मा went with शिव to the sacrificial hall of दक्ष. Now दक्ष began to praise शिव. When विष्णु's offering was poured to secure the continuation of the sacrifice, विष्णु presented himself in person when दक्ष, ऋत्विक्स्, Sadasyas, Rudra and others present, spoke in his praise. Pleased at this, Hari remarked there was no difference among the त्रिमुर्तीस्. दक्ष brought the यज्ञ to a successful end.
8: Ib. IV. 7 (whole); २९. ४२.
--a R. of the केतुमाला. वा. ४४. १९.

son of वर्क्षी (मारिषा-वि। प्।) and Pracetas (प्रा- चेतसष्-वि। प्।); a प्रजापति. He first created the Devas, Asuras, men and others inhabiting the sky, earth and water. Finding the creation incomplete, he went to the Vindhyas for तपस् by bathing in the Agha- मर्षण and propitiating Hari with the hymn of हम्सगुह्य। To him the Lord appeared and urged him to marry असिक्नी, daughter of पञ्चजन and thus increase the created beings.
9: Ib. VI. 4 (whole); Vi. I. १५. १०, ८०-1.
Of असिक्नी he begot १०,000 sons called हर्यश्वस्. The latter proceeded to the western direction to the sacred lake नारायणसरस् at the estuary of the Indus. Purified by the bath and instructed by नारद on the bondage of सम्सार, these took to the path of ‘not returning’ (अन्वर्तन)। दक्ष lamented and begot by the same wife a thousand sons, शबलाश्वस्. These again followed the path trodden by their elder brothers, advised by नारद. The enraged दक्ष cursed that नारद, the corrupter of youth, was ever to be a wanderer and to have no settled home. The sage submitted to it without retaliating.
१०: भा. VI. 5 (whole); Vi. I. १५. ८२-104.
Con- soled by ब्रह्मा, दक्ष further begot sixty daughters of असिक्नी (वैरिनी-म्। प्।). He bestowed ten on Dharma, twelve on कश्यप, twenty-seven on Soma, two each for भूत, Angiras, and कृशाश्व, and the remaining five, of whom only four seem to be named (in v. २१) on तार्क्ष्या.
११: भा. VI. 6 whole; Ib. V. 5. २२; Br. III. 1. 8 and १२; 2. 1-३१; M. १४६. १५-7; भा. III. १४. १२-3; Br. III. 3. 3, 5-५५; 8-5.
Elsewhere it is said that thirteen daughters were given in marriage to कश्यप. [page२-060+ ३५] Went with ब्रह्मा to meet हिरण्यकशिपु; was present at the anointing of वामन; father of Aditi;
१३: भा. VII. 3. १४; VIII. २३. २०; IX. 4. ५४; 1. १०.
cursed Moon god with consumption (यक्ष्म)।
१४: Ib. X. ८८. ३२; XI. 6. ३६.
Wondered at मार्कण्डेय's vrata;
१५: Ib. XII 8. १२.
had not yet seen the Supreme Being; identified with Hari.
१६: Ib. IV. २९. ४२; XI. १६. १५.
Drank of the सौभाग्य from the thigh of Hari and brought forth a daughter सती married by शिव;
१७: M. ६०. 6-7, १०-11; १४५. ९०.
a महऋषि; heard the पुराण from ब्रह्मा along with other sages;
१८: Vi. I. 2. 8.
son of ब्रह्मा, married ऊर्जा.
१९: Ib. I. 7. 5-7.
^१२) M. २३. १५;

(II)--in previous birth son of ब्रह्मा, now born of मारिषा and Pracetasas. Was made a chief progeni- tor on the eve of the चाक्षुष epoch;
1: भा. IV. ३०. ४९-51; Br. IV. 1. २४, ३९-44.
a grandson of Soma; created men with two feet and four feet, of different faces, ears, etc., also म्लेच्छस् and women; also produced १००० sons with पाञ्चजनि, named हर्यश्वस्. नारद asked them to go into the world over but they perished in their sojourn. So he begot another १००० of वैरिणी, and these were शबलस् set by नारद in quest of the whereabouts of their brothers. They also perished.
2: M. 4. ४९-55; 5. 2-१४.
(III)--the son of Citrasena, and father of मीढ्वान्. भा. IX. 2. १९. [page२-061+ ३२]
(IV)--a son of उशीनर. भा. IX. २३. 3.

(V)--created from प्राण, half तेजस् of Pracetas and half of Soma; created creatures, two-legged and four- legged, in the Vaivasvata epoch;
1: Br. I. 5. ७०; वा. ६३. ३५-48; ६५. १२१-158.
Lord of प्रजापतिस्.
2: वा. ७०-5; १०१. ३५, ४९.
Got प्राचेतसत्वम् in the epoch of चाक्षुष by the curse of Trayambaka; father-in-law of the seven sages.
3: Br. II. १३. ४०-69.
(VI)--an Asura, and a son of बाष्कल. Br. III. 5. ३८.
(VII)--Heard the पुराण from तृणबिन्दु and narrated it to शक्ति. Br. IV. 4. ६५.
(VIII)--a son of देवातीथि. M. ५०. ३७.
(IX)--a son of भृगु; one of the twelve विश्वे- devas. M. १९५. १३; २०३. १३; वा. ६६. ३१.

(X)--a son of Angirasa;
1: M. १९६. 2; वा. ६५. १०५.
through his daughter a son, प्रियाय.
2: वा. १००. २४.
(XI)--a pravara sage. M. १९६. ३०.
(XII)--with the sun in the months of माघ and फाल्गुन. वा. ५२. २३.
(XIII)--a son of Jambha. वा. ६७. ७८. [page२-062+ २६]
--given by स्वायम्भुव Manu to Atri. वा. ६२. ७३.
--bathed King Gaya with the waters. भा. V. १५. १०.

--the ninth Manu born of वरुण.
1: भा. VIII. १३. १८.
Three groups of twelve gods in each of पार, मारीचिगर्भ and सुधर्मान. Their Indra was Adbhuta. Savana, Dyu- timan and others were seven sages. Father of धृतिकेतु and other sons.
2: Vi. III. 2. २०-24.
--a kingdom through which ऋसभ passed. भा. V. 6. 7.
--a R. of the South. वा. ७७. 8.
--the country to which पुरञ्जन went by the entrance of the पितृस्, allegorically प्रवृत्तिशास्त्र. भा. IV. २५. ५०; २९. १३.
--the southern route to the abode of Yama: the place for burial grounds. Br. II. २७. १२५; ३५. १४७; वा. ६१. १२३.
--(Taijasa bandha in other books). वा. १०२. ५९. [page२-063+ २४]
--a तीर्थ; from उत्तरमानस one should go to दक्षिणमानस in silence and thence to उदीची- तीर्थम् where there are three तीर्थस्. वा. १११. 6-8.
--of three streets, अजवीथि and the street of constellations श्रवण, धनिष्ठ and सतभिषक् and the street of वैश्वानरी, भाद्रपद and रेवती. Br. III. 3. ५३.
--generally the southern people. Vi. II. 3. १६.
--as sister and wife of यज्ञ and mother of १२ Ya1ma1 gods. Vi. I. 7. २१.

--a daughter of Ruci and आकूती; consort of सुयज्ञ, an अवतार् of Hari. Had twelve sons who were known as तुषित gods (यामस्) of the period of स्वायम्- bhuva Manu. भा. II. 7. 2; IV. 1. 5-8; Br. II. 9. ४४.
--represents the face of the Veda. वा. १०४. ८५.
--the Malaya hill; residence of Agastya. M. ६१. ४०. [page२-064+ ३५]

--a kingdom over which the three sons of Sudyumna ruled;
1: भा. IX. 1. ४१.
includes the नर्मदा region;
2: Br. III. १०. ९८; ६३. 9-१०; M. १५. २८; ११४. २९; वा. ४५. १२४.
ruled over by about twenty (forty-eight-वि। प्।) of इक्ष्वा- ku's sons.
3: वा. ८८. ११; Vi. IV. 2. १४.
गार्ग्य's place of penance.
4: Vi. V. २३. 2.

--The sun moves fast in;
1: वा. ५०. ९२, १३६; ५१. ७३.
moves in the midst of पुष्करद्वीप.
2: Br. II. २१. ३५-6. Ib. II. २१. ६७.
--the southern Sun at नैमिष. वा. १०९. २१.
--the Bay of Bengal. M. १२१. ४४.
--evil spirits injuring children. भा. X. 6. २७; ६३. १०.
--a काश्यप gotraka1ra. M. १९९. 5.
(I)--a son of दारुक, an अवतार् of the Lord. वा. २३. १९६.
--a sage; a त्रयार्षेय pravara. M. १९६. २५; १९७. 6.

--(द्राविडस्); southerners;
1: Br. II. ३१. ८२; वा. ५८. ८२; ९८. १०७.
to be conquer- ed by Kalki.
